thread:
devon: heads up — Saga Commerce is seeing a wave of 5xx + timeouts from hosted API in eu-west-1. customer_traffic spike ~200k reqs in 10m, lots of p95s and 504s. filing here for triage.
nana: ack. do we have a short repro or request samples?
devon: pasted a failing curl from their support ticket below and a snippet from gateway logs. they report errors start ~2026-03-18T09:04Z.
devon: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"gpt-like-xxl","input":"summarize..."}'```
devon: gateway logs: `ingress: tenant=saga-commerce req=0x8f3 status=504 queue_wait=1450ms batch_wait=1200ms route=hosted-eu-west`
support_jen: customer provided timestamps and request ids, I'll attach. they see timeouts even on small prompts.
mike_oncall: looking at dashboards now. p95 token latency spiking coincident with request queue depth hitting 512 on several frontends. continuous-batcher backlog metric shows ~3k enqueued across pool.
mike_oncall: also seeing kvcache churn — miss rate up 20%. possible cache warmup + big tenant burst causing batching backlog.
nana: any recent deploys to batching runtime?
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy to cbatch-runtime v1.12 completed 2026-03-18T08:58Z by @infra-ci. no rollback.
mike_oncall: no obvious bad deploy but the burst is large. suspect queue-depth limit + tenant burst causing long head-of-line waits. many requests keep getting continuous-batcher backoff and fall through to gateway 504.
devon: customer says errors started after they pushed a marketing campaign, mass concurrent calls with identical prompt prefix. they also use streaming which increases open connections.
nana: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle tenant at ingress (soft drop) 2) reduce continuous-batcher max_batch_ms on eu-west pool 3) temporarily route saga-commerce to a smaller instance pool (dedicated) or fallback model. agree?
mike_oncall: doing (1) now — applying tenant rate limit: `tenant_rate_limit.saga-commerce=500rps` to stop tail-surge.
mike_oncall: (2) lowering max_batch_ms from 50 -> 20 on cbatch workers in eu-west. patching config...
mike_oncall: (3) opened a routing rule to prefer smaller quantized variant `gpt-like-xxl-q4` if queue_wait > 800ms.
devon: thanks. can we also flush kvcache entries for that tenant? cache eviction seems noisy.
sre-bot: cache-tool: evict-tenant saga-commerce kvcache shards 3/3 — started.
nana: support_jen, pls tell customer we applied a soft throttle and a fallback; ask them to retry and send any request ids that still fail.
support_jen: on it. pinged Saga account team and sent escalation note.
devon: monitoring now — queue depth dropped to ~120 within 30s, 5xxs falling. p95 latency improving from 1.8s -> 420ms.
mike_oncall: still watching KV miss rate — may need kvcache sizing tweaks or prewarm for large tenants. filing infra follow-up ticket: INFRA-2026-kvcache-sizing-saga-commerce.
nana: please record a short repro for postmortem: steps, tenant load shape, exact payload (they said identical prompt prefix), and any config we changed.
devon: repro notes: send 60k concurrent very short requests over 5m with same prefix + streaming flag -> queue depth climbs, batcher stalls at 50ms max_batch and queue_wait grows -> gateway 504.
support_jen: customer confirmed reduced errors after our throttle. they're happy for now but want plan to avoid throttles in future.
mike_oncall: follow-ups: (A) recommend tenant-level prewarm/ratelimit rules for marketing bursts (B) autoscale continuous-batcher pool by queue depth, (C) improve kvcache hot-key handling and prewarming API.
nana: I'll draft the postmortem and action items. thanks all for the quick response. :thumbsup:
devon: adding note to incident timeline and tagging product ops for customer communication.
sre-bot: incident-logger: event recorded incident=1767777766 severity=high mitigation=tenant-throttle+fallback
ana: closing thread for now; reopen if errors return.
